tema: Umbrella review of the dominant aetiological views in fibromyalgia, IBS, CFS/ME and somatic symptom disorders.
diseno: Umbrella review of 452 reviews (132 systematic with meta-analysis, 133 systematic, 197 narrative) in PubMed, Web of Science, Embase and PsycINFO.
hallazgos: Biological factors were addressed in 90% of the reviews, psychological factors in 33%, social factors in 12% and health-system factors in 5%; methodological quality was mostly low or moderate; high-quality reviews point to immune, endocrine, genetic, neurological and psychosocial factors.
conclusion: Very few reviews use comprehensive biopsychosocial models; future research must raise its standards and broaden the perspective on these conditions.
triangulacion: Abstract and conclusions (taken from the abstract itself) agree; the keywords emphasize the framing of functional somatic syndromes and somatoform disorders, consistent with the review's psychiatric perspective.

tema: Investigates changes in cortical volume and thickness in ME/CFS compared with healthy controls and their relationship to clinical measures.
diseno: Cross-sectional study with MRI and FreeSurfer in 18 patients (ICC criteria) and 26 healthy controls; vertex-wise analysis, subcortical volumes and group-interaction regressions.
hallazgos: Reduced thickness in the caudal middle frontal gyrus (p = 0.0016) and the precuneus (p = 0.013), and greater amygdala volume (p = 0.002) in ME/CFS. Regressions with fatigue, heart rate variability, sleep, respiratory rate and cognition were abnormal.
conclusion: The authors conclude that cortical volume and thickness are altered in ME/CFS and that their relationship to key symptoms is abnormal.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusions are fully consistent (precuneus, amygdala, cortical thickness); the conclusions repeat the abstract without additional nuance.

tema: Explores the effect of Tai Chi Chuan on effective connectivity between resting-state brain networks in patients with CFS.
diseno: Pre-post intervention study with rs-fMRI and SF-36 in 21 CFS patients and 19 healthy controls, before and after 1 month of Tai Chi Chuan; independent component analysis and Granger causality.
hallazgos: At baseline, patients had worse SF-36 scores and a weakened causal relationship between the sensorimotor network (SMN) and the default mode network (DMN), which improved after training. This relationship correlated with physical role and bodily pain, and its change with the change in pain.
conclusion: Tai Chi Chuan could improve quality of life and promote brain network plasticity; SMN-DMN Granger causality could be a readout parameter for CFS.
triangulacion: The three sources agree on SMN, DMN and Granger causality; the abstract states improvement in quality of life, whereas the conclusions focus on connectivity, with no active control group.

tema: To characterize fatty acid oxidation in NK cells, CD4+ T cells and CD8+ T cells from ME/CFS patients.
diseno: Ex vivo experimental study with samples from 8 to 20 subjects per experiment; perturbations of fatty acid oxidation at rest and after stimulation.
hallazgos: All three cell types increased their use of lipids and the proteins of this pathway, especially with higher energy demand; in CD4+ cells fatty acid utilization correlated with disease duration.
conclusion: Supports an altered bioenergetic state in immune cells; NK dysfunction could be due in part to lipid accumulation and the T cell profile would suggest exhaustion.
triangulacion: Consistent; the conclusions advance the T cell exhaustion hypothesis, presented in the abstract only as speculation.

tema: Analyses circulating microRNAs that regulate the Sirt1/eNOS axis as possible biomarkers of endothelial dysfunction in ME/CFS.
diseno: Case-control study in plasma of ME/CFS patients versus healthy controls (sample size not stated in the text), with validation in public PBMC miR data and bioinformatic analysis of networks and pathways.
hallazgos: miR-21, miR-34a, miR-92a, miR-126 and miR-200c were jointly increased in patients, a finding replicated in public PBMC data. The associated pathways include endothelial function, oxidative stress and oxygen regulation; histone deacetylase 1 was the most relevant node of the network.
conclusion: The study lays the groundwork for biomarkers of endothelial dysfunction; the authors propose combining FMD/EndoPAT with these miRs to stratify patients, although they acknowledge they are not yet translatable to the clinic.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and discussion are consistent on the endothelium-NO-oxidative stress axis; the discussion is more cautious, calling for larger cohorts with follow-up and diagnostic criteria stricter than Fukuda.

tema: Characterizes B lymphocyte subpopulations in CFS patients compared with healthy controls, motivated by the response to rituximab.
diseno: Case-control study: 33 patients meeting Canadian and Fukuda criteria and 24 matched controls; extended B lymphocyte immunophenotyping by flow cytometry.
hallazgos: Patients had more naïve B lymphocytes (65% vs 47% of B cells; P = 0.003), more transitional B cells (1.8% vs 0.8%; P = 0.025) and fewer plasmablasts (0.5% vs 0.9%; P = 0.013).
conclusion: The changes could suggest a subtle tendency toward autoimmunity, although it cannot be determined whether they cause the symptoms or derive from inactivity, sleep disturbance or stress.
triangulacion: The three sources agree on the alterations in B subpopulations; the conclusions (from the discussion) are more cautious about causality and relate transitional B cells to lymphadenopathy.

tema: Systematic review of exercise-induced immunological changes in CFS patients compared with healthy controls.
diseno: Systematic review in PubMed and Web of Science; number of studies not stated.
hallazgos: Compared with sedentary controls, patients showed a more pronounced response of complement (C4a), of oxidative stress (with a delayed and reduced antioxidant response) and of IL-10 and TLR4 gene expression after exercise, but not of circulating cytokines.
conclusion: There is an altered immune response to exercise in CFS, related to post-exertional malaise; experimental designs, other tissues and control of covariates are needed.
triangulacion: Abstract and conclusions are consistent, but the title (exercise in extreme environments) and the keywords (salivary lysozyme, thermal stress, runners) correspond to another work, indicating a metadata error.

tema: To analyse muscle membrane excitability and redox state to differentiate ME/CFS subgroups.
diseno: Study in 72 patients at rest, incremental cycle ergometer exercise and recovery; recording of M-wave, TBARS, ORP and plasma potassium.
hallazgos: 39 patients showed marked M-wave alterations, elevated TBARS and ORP and lower K+ efflux; 33 had no alterations and had lower oxidative stress; M-wave changes were inversely proportional to TBARS and ORP.
conclusion: There is altered membrane excitability and biomarker heterogeneity; ORP measurement could help diagnosis.
triangulacion: Consistent on redox stress, M-wave and heterogeneity; the conclusions stress the need for studies in other populations.

tema: To propose an explainable AI model to predict ME/CFS and identify discriminating metabolites.
diseno: Analysis of a metabolomic dataset of 26 patients and 26 controls (768 metabolites); random forest and other classifiers; hold-out, cross and bootstrap validation; XAI.
hallazgos: C-glycosyltryptophan, oleoylcholine, cortisone and 3-hydroxydecanoate were key; random forest reached 98% accuracy and 99% AUC with bootstrap.
conclusion: The model classifies patients accurately and offers risk interpretation useful for clinicians.
triangulacion: Consistent; the conclusions add limitations (lack of independent biological verification, need for multicentre validation and more samples), which qualify the high figures obtained with a small sample.

tema: To measure mitochondrial function and the detection of energy stress in immortalized lymphoblasts from ME/CFS patients.
diseno: Case-control with lymphoblasts from 51 patients (Canadian Criteria) and matched controls; Seahorse, proteomics and biochemical assays.
hallazgos: ATP synthesis by Complex V reduced in proportion to basal OCR; elevated Complex I OCR, maximal and spare capacity and proton leak; lower membrane potential and hyperactivated TORC1; normal resting ATP.
conclusion: Isolated Complex V defect with compensation that normalizes resting ATP but would limit the response to acute increases in demand; the abnormalities correlate with severity.
triangulacion: Consistent, with keywords that link to PEM; the conclusions add the correlation with symptom severity and its potential as a biomarker.

tema: Defines chronotropic incompetence/intolerance and synthesizes the heart rate response during maximal CPET in ME/CFS.
diseno: Review with a systematic review and meta-analysis of published studies with maximal CPET in ME/CFS; pooled size not stated.
hallazgos: The literature consistently shows an attenuated increase in heart rate during CPET in ME/CFS, both at maximal effort and at the ventilatory threshold (VAT), compatible with chronotropic intolerance and lower cardiac output.
conclusion: There is an abnormally attenuated chronotropic response in ME/CFS that points to autonomic dysregulation; tests or pacing plans based on percentages of predicted maximum heart rate should be treated with caution because of the risk of supramaximal effort.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusions agree on chronotropic intolerance and CPET. The conclusions add clinical implications (pacing, submaximal tests) that the abstract only announces as an aim.

tema: Reviews clinical trials of pharmacological interventions and supplements in ME/CFS and proposes recommendations for future trials.
diseno: Narrative review of clinical trials from the last 33 years targeting immunological, metabolic, gastrointestinal, neurological and neuroendocrine dysfunction.
hallazgos: Fewer than 5% of patients recover their pre-morbid activity; rintatolimod is the only example of a successful treatment but remains experimental; antivirals (valacyclovir, valganciclovir, artesunate), metabolic supplements and probiotics show promising results.
conclusion: More powerful trials are needed with objective measures (accelerometers), uniform clinical subtypes and strict case definitions that include PEM; repositioning drugs such as luteolin or mast cell stabilizers is suggested.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent; the conclusions specify what the abstract only announces (rintatolimod, antivirals, accelerometers, PEM as a criterion).

tema: Deduces the pathophysiological mechanisms that would explain the central nervous system pathology and the neurocognitive symptoms of ME/CFS.
diseno: Theoretical article based on the evidence on endothelial dysfunction and muscle and cerebral hypoperfusion; no own empirical data.
hallazgos: Tentative mechanisms described are reduced cerebral blood flow, altered neurovascular coupling, central adrenergic hyperactivity, hypocapnia and increased intracranial pressure.
conclusion: These mechanisms could explain cognitive impairment, brain fog, headache, hypersensitivity, sleep disorders and dysautonomia; whether neuroinflammation or brainstem pathology exists remains to be demonstrated.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent around cerebral hypoperfusion and endothelial dysfunction; the conclusions add caution by noting that no specific brain pathology has been detected.

tema: Explores HRV measured with mHealth technology as an objective marker of ME/CFS and assesses gender differences in HRV and core symptoms.
diseno: Case-control study with 77 patients (32 men, 45 women) and 44 healthy controls; questionnaires on fatigue, sleep, anxiety, depression and autonomic symptoms; recording of RR intervals in three 5-min periods with a chest strap and iOS app; MANOVA.
hallazgos: Men with ME/CFS scored higher on all symptoms, with no HRV differences compared with controls (unlike women), although with negative correlations between symptoms and SDNN, RMSSD, pNN50 and LF. There were gender effects on HF, LF/HF and HFnu, and lower HRV in women with ME/CFS than in men.
conclusion: HRV through mHealth is an objective, non-invasive tool useful for diagnosis, monitoring and prediction of fatigue severity, especially in women with ME/CFS.
triangulacion: The sources are consistent on the HRV-mHealth-gender focus; the PDF conclusions add the diagnostic use and call for more studies to corroborate the gender differences.

tema: Describes a case of vasospastic or microvascular angina diagnosed simultaneously with the recurrence and worsening of ME/CFS, and warns about cardiac ischaemia in these patients.
diseno: Case report of a young woman with ME/CFS and new-onset angina.
hallazgos: The anginal symptoms (exertional chest pain and transient chest discomfort) mimicked those of ME/CFS and were relieved after a calcium antagonist was administered.
conclusion: Cardiac manifestations can appear with the worsening of ME/CFS and angina can go unnoticed because its symptoms overlap; the authors recommend cardiac examinations, including ECG, also in the face of excessive exhaustion.
triangulacion: The three sources agree on microvascular/vasospastic angina and endothelial dysfunction as the link; the discussion (with noise from final declarations) reinforces the recommendation of cardiac screening, more explicit than in the abstract.

tema: Systematic review of genetic studies of COVID-19 and ME/CFS to identify common genetic components.
diseno: Review of genetic association and cohort studies (71 on COVID-19 and 26 on ME/CFS), with gene ontology and pathway analysis using PANTHER 17.0.
hallazgos: 97 affected genes were identified in COVID-19 and 429 in ME/CFS. The common genes were ACE, HLA-A, HLA-C, HLA-DQA1, HLA-DRB1 and TYK2, with pathways of chemokine- and cytokine-mediated inflammation, T cell activation and Toll receptors.
conclusion: Despite similar symptoms, the two diseases share few genes, all linked to immune regulation. The pathogenesis of both could derive from an aberrant and persistent immune response, perhaps involving mast cells and microglia.
triangulacion: The three sources agree on ACE, HLA and immune dysfunction. The conclusions stress that the genetic overlap is small (a nuance less visible in the abstract) and add the mast cell and microglia hypothesis.

tema: Seeks to confirm the anticorrelation between subcortical and sensorimotor myelination in humans as evidence of a regulatory process.
diseno: Analysis of nine image sets from three cohorts with six myelin-sensitive MRI modalities, each with healthy controls and subjects with ME/CFS; optimized ROIs and correlations between regions.
hallazgos: In healthy controls, negative subcortical-sensorimotor correlations were confirmed in six sets (T1wSE, T2wSE, MTC and white matter volume); T1/T2 was the exception with a positive correlation.
conclusion: The authors propose a regulatory mechanism in which low subcortical myelination (brainstem, reticular activating system) is compensated by greater sensorimotor myelination, mediated by a thalamus-interneuron oscillator circuit.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusions are consistent on myelination and anticorrelation; although the keywords mention CFS and multiple sclerosis, the focus is physiological in healthy controls and ME/CFS is hardly discussed.

tema: Looks for serological evidence of past infection or reactivation by human herpesviruses (HHV-1 to 7) in ME/CFS cohorts.
diseno: Case-control study: several cohorts of patients meeting Canadian criteria versus Swedish blood donors; multiplex suspension immunoassay (SMIA) of IgG with whole viruses, recombinant proteins and synthetic peptides. Sample size not stated.
hallazgos: Overall IgG reactivity against herpesviruses did not differ between patients and controls; minor relative differences were observed against HHV-1 antigens and EBV EBNA6 and EA, and new epitope information was obtained.
conclusion: Herpesvirus infections are not more common or intense in ME/CFS, but the subtle differences, which should not be over-interpreted, suggest that the immune system of some patients interacts differently with these viruses.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent; abstract and conclusions keep a cautious tone about the minor differences. The keywords adequately reflect the viruses studied.

tema: Analyses autoantibodies against β-adrenergic and cholinergic muscarinic receptors in CFS and their relationship to the response to rituximab.
diseno: Case-control study: Berlin cohort (n=268) and 25 patients from the KTS-2 rituximab trial (Bergen) with pre- and post-treatment samples, versus 108 controls; IgG against multiple G protein-coupled receptors by ELISA.
hallazgos: Antibodies against β2, M3 and M4 were elevated in patients; they correlated with IgG1-3 subclasses, activation of HLA-DR+ T cells and anti-thyroid peroxidase and antinuclear antibodies; they decreased in rituximab responders; 29.5% had elevated antibodies.
conclusion: A subgroup of patients has autoantibodies against β2 AdR and M AChR receptors, which could play a pathogenic role and serve as biomarkers in B cell depletion trials.
triangulacion: The three sources agree; the conclusions (from the discussion) are more cautious than the abstract in stating that the function of the antibodies is unclear. They include conflicts of interest because of patents.

tema: Explores FGF21 and NT-proBNP as possible biomarkers in ME/CFS and their relationship to oxidative stress and inflammation.
diseno: Case-control study: 21 patients and 20 matched controls; validated questionnaires and plasma measurement of antioxidant capacity, lipoperoxides, cytokines, CRP, FGF21 and NT-proBNP.
hallazgos: Patients showed lower total antioxidant capacity and more lipoperoxides, higher IL-1β, IL-6, IL-10, TNF-α and CRP (not IL-8), and higher levels of FGF21 (p < 0.0001) and NT-proBNP (p = 0.005); NT-proBNP correlated with IL-1β and IL-6.
conclusion: Elevated FGF21 and NT-proBNP, and the association of NT-proBNP with inflammation, could be new diagnostic and therapeutic targets.
triangulacion: Keywords and abstract are consistent (oxidative stress, low-grade inflammation); the extracted conclusions text is noise (declarations and abbreviations), so there are no conclusions of its own to compare.

tema: To review the effect of probiotic treatments in patients with fibromyalgia or CFS.
diseno: Systematic review in 14 databases (2006-2016) of RCTs and pilot studies; Jadad scale; 2 studies included (n=83), both in CFS.
hallazgos: Lactobacillus casei Shirota reduced anxiety and modified faecal composition; Bifidobacterium infantis 35624 reduced inflammatory biomarkers, both within 8 weeks.
conclusion: Some strains show beneficial effects in CFS, but the evidence is limited and there are no studies in fibromyalgia.
triangulacion: Consistent; the conclusions are somewhat more optimistic and speculate on emotional and cognitive benefits that were not assessed.

tema: Investigates whether there are specific sleep phenotypes in CFS and which objective characteristics differentiate them.
diseno: Single-centre cross-sectional study at a fatigue clinic in the Netherlands; 343 consecutive CFS patients (Fukuda criteria); one night of blind-scored polysomnography; hierarchical cluster analysis and ANOVA.
hallazgos: 30.3% (104) had a primary sleep disorder that explained the diagnosis. In the remaining 239, four sleep phenotypes were identified and 89.1% met criteria for at least one objective sleep problem; the phenotypes were distinguished by sleep and REM latencies, awakenings, total sleep time and wake after sleep onset.
conclusion: It is necessary to systematically screen for primary sleep disorders and to tailor sleep interventions to the phenotype in CFS patients.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent; the conclusions come from the structured abstract and reproduce it. The keywords capture phenotypes, primary sleep disorders and REM latency.

tema: Explores whether there are CFS subgroups in adolescents based on biological markers and their relationship to other variables.
diseno: Hierarchical cluster analysis (Ward's method) in 116 adolescents with CFS (NorCAPITAL cohort, broad criteria) with immunological, autonomic, neuroendocrine, cognitive and sensory variables.
hallazgos: Six clusters were delineated (e.g., orthostatic intolerance, low-grade inflammation, high vagal activity) with substantial overlap; only the cluster of pain intolerance and poor cognition was associated with worse function, quality of life and Canada 2003 criteria.
conclusion: Clusters can be delineated but not distinct subgroups; the results question the clinical usefulness of looking for subgroups and the validity of the stricter diagnostic criteria.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent; the conclusions repeat the abstract. The keywords (HPA axis, orthostatic intolerance) reflect the biological domains analysed.

tema: To evaluate the reliability and reproducibility of the commercial mitochondrial energy score (MES) test as a diagnostic test for ME/CFS.
diseno: Replication of the MES protocol in neutrophils and PBMC from 10 patients and 13 controls; test of the effect of delaying processing by 24 h.
hallazgos: There were no differences between patients and controls in any MES component (p ≥ 0.059); delaying processing by 24 h significantly altered many parameters.
conclusion: The MES lacks reliability and reproducibility and should not be offered as a diagnostic test; previous differences could be due to processing time.
triangulacion: Keywords and abstract are consistent (reliability, processing time); the conclusions text is actually the methods section (noise), providing no comparison.

tema: Evaluates the diagnostic value of PBMC and extracellular vesicle microRNA profiles in severe ME/CFS.
diseno: Case-control study with severe patients from the UK ME Biobank, standard operating procedures (SOPs) and miRNA profiles (Nanostring) in PBMC and extracellular vesicles, together with laboratory tests and physical characteristics of the vesicles; ROC curves. Sample size not stated.
hallazgos: Creatine kinase (CK), the characteristics of plasma vesicles (number, size and zeta potential) and a few differentially expressed miRNAs were significantly associated with severe ME/CFS (p < 0.05). Gene enrichment pointed to epigenetic and neuroimmune pathways.
conclusion: The authors argue for validating these few discriminating variables at population level through a cost-effective approach.
triangulacion: Keywords and abstract agree (miRNA, extracellular vesicles, diagnostic biomarkers). The conclusions text (discussion) is methodological (statistical analysis, data availability) and provides no conclusions.
